# The Necronomicon
[color=#999999][italic]"Join us..."[/italic][/color]
As the shift starts, an antique tape recorder somewhere aboard, centuries old, finishes reading from the [color=#a01818]Necronomicon Ex-Mortis[/color], the Book of the Dead: Sumerian, written by the Dark Ones, bound in human flesh and inked in blood. Something answers: a [color=#a01818]Kandarian Demon[/color]. The Kandarian dagger lies beside the recorder: strike a downed Deadite with it and it's cut apart for good, and it bites deep into the demon's flesh. Play the recorder (or rewind it) to hear the log of the archaeologist who recorded it.
## For the crew - [bold]The book is the demon's anchor, and it can't be destroyed.[/bold] Burn it (keep it burning for about twenty seconds) and it's torn back into the ether for three minutes, its demon loses half its Soul Power and every Deadite is thrown to the floor. But it knits itself back together. Fire buys time; it doesn't win. - [bold]Klaatu. Barada. Nikto.[/bold] Say the words, every one of them, within a few tiles of the book before you pick it up. Take it without them, or fumble them, and the book bites, the demon grows stronger, every downed Deadite gets back up and you are left open to possession. This happens once each time the book comes into the world. - [bold]Find the lost pages.[/bold] The archaeologist who first translated the book tore out two passages; they're hidden somewhere aboard. Holding them with the book nearby, alt-click them to recite. The first conjures the evil into the flesh (it's dragged into its body and can't leave it for three minutes). The second opens a rift that swallows the demon and the book, if the demon's body is close. [bold]This is the only way to beat the Necronomicon.[/bold] Every possessed person is freed, alive, and the shift goes on. - [bold]Read from it.[/bold] It's written in blood in a language nobody living understands, but a long-dead archaeologist's pencilled notes explain a few pages. With the book in your hand, right-click someone to read the [bold]Passage of Rebuking[/bold] (casts a Deadite out of its host; the Deadite can barely move while you read) or a Demonspawn to read the [bold]Passage of Unmaking[/bold]. Alt-click the book to read aloud from a random page and gamble. Every reading draws blood, leaves you open to JOIN US unless you're mindshielded, warns the demon, and the book has to rest for a minute afterwards. - [bold]Hold onto it.[/bold] While a living, unpossessed person carries the book (in hand, a pocket or a bag), it [italic]cannot[/italic] vanish back into the ether. - [bold]Anyone could be a Deadite.[/bold] They look completely normal until they reveal themselves. Then their skin goes corpse-pale, their eyes turn milky white and they start screaming. - A revealed Deadite floats up off the floor, talks normally, taunts ("Join us!", "Dead by dawn!") and its laughs, screams and snarls are unmistakable. The possessed don't die by ordinary means: beat one into critical and it gets back up shortly after. Only dismemberment stops it: a heavy slash while it's down takes its head, and it stays down. Burning the book ends them all. - [bold]Brujo talismans[/bold] (two are hidden aboard) ward whoever carries one or stands next to one: JOIN US, possession, bites and the demon's powers slide off. Each block burns it; it crumbles after three. - [bold]Mindshields[/bold] protect against possession, until a revealed Deadite reads the passage that melts them away. - [bold]Chaplains can exorcise Deadites.[/bold] Cuff, buckle or down the suspect, then use the [bold]Exorcise[/bold] verb with a Bible in hand and stand still for about twenty seconds. A Deadite comes back as themselves, healed, and the book can't claim them again for ten minutes. A mindshield implanted in the Deadite first halves the time. Anyone else is unharmed: the rite simply finds nothing. The chaplain needs a short rest between rites. - [bold]Demonspawn[/bold] grow into tall, grey, black-eyed adults after ten minutes. Both forms are [color=#88bbff]melted to dust[/color] by holy water (splash or spray it) or a Bible (hit them with it, use it on them or throw it).
## For the demon - Before the round, pick your [bold]alias[/bold], your [bold]form[/bold] (Abomination, Hellspawn, Flesh Golem, Wraith, Shambling Lover, Crawler or Apparition) and your [bold]aura[/bold] colour in Character Setup → Antags → Kandarian Demon → Loadout. Each form has its own speed, toughness and claws. - You start [bold]incorporeal[/bold]: invisible to the living, untouchable and unable to touch anything. - Powers bought in the store: [bold]Voices in the Dark[/bold] (whispers), [bold]The Laughing Room[/bold] (lights flicker, furniture laughs), [bold]The Force[/bold] (charge through the station, flattening people), [bold]The Trees[/bold] (roots hold a victim), [bold]The Hand[/bold] (a victim's hand turns on them), [bold]False Eyes[/bold] (make someone see a friend's eyes flash white), [bold]Possessed Puppet[/bold] and [bold]Dead by Dawn[/bold] (every Deadite rises, healed and fast). - Servants: [bold]From the Grave[/bold] (raise a corpse as a Deadite, played by a ghost if nobody's in it), [bold]Call Up the Wicked Dead[/bold] (one of the wicked dead dragged out of Hell into a body: a huge, ghost-controlled Deadite) and the [bold]Army of the Dead[/bold] (deadite skeletons). - Revealed Deadites can [bold]Swallow Their Soul[/bold]: feed on someone down and dying to heal and feed the book. - [bold]Soul Power[/bold] comes from fear: monsters near the crew, monsters speaking, attacks, witnesses and supernatural events. Spend it in the [bold]Skill Store[/bold]. - [bold]Manifest Necronomicon[/bold] puts the book in the world where you stand. JOIN US reaches 12 tiles from you while the book is in the world, and possession needs the victim within 20 tiles of the book (they can run while it happens). - [bold]JOIN US[/bold] prepares a victim (a Deadite bite does too). [bold]Possess[/bold] then turns them into a disguised Deadite and uses a charge. You start with two. - [bold]Demonic Possession[/bold] is harmless: the victim collapses and your words come out of their mouth. With [bold]Speak to the Station[/bold], your next sentence becomes an announcement in their name. - [bold]Physical Form[/bold] lets you walk the station in your chosen shape, under your own name. In the body your ether powers sleep; instead you have [bold]Unholy Roar[/bold] (knocks nearby crew down), [bold]Poltergeist[/bold] (hurls loose objects at the nearest person) and [bold]Return to the Ether[/bold]. If the body falls, you return to the ether. - Possessions, Deadites rising, rituals and manifestations make [bold]lights flicker and objects fly[/bold], and the old words ([italic]Kanda... Estrada... Amantos...[/italic]) rise around the victim. A victim being possessed is pinned to the floor until it's over. - [bold]Deadite Evolution[/bold] in the store improves all your Deadites, present and future. Pick two of four paths, each with two tiers: [bold]Infiltrator[/bold] (silent bites, slower exorcisms, hiding again after revealing), [bold]Brute[/bold] (harder hits, faster recovery, damage resistance), [bold]Stalker[/bold] (speed, longer bites, crippling bites) or [bold]Screamer[/bold] (a terrifying shriek that can knock people down). - Your HUD shows your Soul Power, your charges and where your book is. Talk privately with other Kandarian entities using [bold]:k[/bold] (Ancient Sumerian).
## Victory The Necronomicon wins when every living person aboard (connected or not) has been claimed or killed. The crew beats it only by opening the rift; the demon is cast out, but the round carries on. The round-end summary lists souls consumed, possessions, Deadites, Demonspawn, fear harvested, rituals, exorcisms and how long the demon lasted.
